newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Deceuninck surges to new high.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Deceuninck surges to new high.

text.p: Belgian plastics processor Deceuninck surged on the Brussels bourse on Thursday, but traders were at a loss to say why.

"I have no idea why the share is so strong," one trader said. "It could be the PVC deal it just did in the United States. It could be that the market is illiquid and there has been some buying from Britain which will push prices up."
At 1100 GMT the share was 300 francs or four percent up at 6,600 having earlier hit a new high of 6,780 francs. Volume was 4,442 shares.
Deceuninck said earlier this week it had bought leading U.S. PVC producer Dayton Technologies from Alcoa.
"PVC is getting more supporters in the United States," the trader said. "It is a growth market."
However, other traders speculated that Deceuninck's major shareholders may be reviewing their industrial holdings with a view to a sale.
Deceuninck is controlled by Royale Vendome which is itself a joint venture between France's Union des Assurances de Paris (UAP) and Belgium's Groupe Bruxelles Lambert.
Analysts have speculated that UAP's recent merger with French insurer AXA to form AXA-UAP may lead it to focus on its core activities and offload industrials.
"It is possible that there is speculation the stake will be sold," one trader said. "But that is just a theory."
Traders also said there were continuous rumours Deceuninck itself might be the target of a takeover bid, although they noted that the firm itself consistently rejected the possibility.
No one was avaialable for comment at Deceuninck's Brussels headquarters.
